neighbours.label: the dots of a spaced ellipsis ' . . .' marking a trailing-off hesitation (strongest on the last dot)
fire: When he finally opened the box . . . it was completely empty.
We drove for hours, and then . . . nothing, just sand.
She looked at me and whispered, "I . . . I can't do this."
I was going to call you, but . . . well, you know how it is.
The answer, my friends, is . . . no one really knows.
He opened his mouth and . . . and no words came out.
So that . . . I don't know what that means, honestly.
The door creaked, the lights flickered . . . and then silence.
quiet: When he finally opened the box, it was completely empty.
We drove for hours, and then we stopped for gas and sandwiches.
She looked at me and whispered, "I can't do this."
I was going to call you, but... well, you know how it is.
The answer, my friends, is that no one really knows.
He opened his mouth... and no words came out.
So that is what it means, honestly, in the end.
The door creaked, the lights flickered, and then there was silence.
